nodes.name: Pristine NiFe LDH hydrothermal synthesis
nodes.procedure: NiCl₂·6H₂O (3 mmol), Fe(NO₃)₃·9H₂O (1 mmol), urea (20 mmol), and NH₄F (10 mmol) were dissolved in 21 mL of water. Subsequently, the resulting mixture was transferred into a 30 mL Teflon-lined autoclave and subjected to heating in an oven at 120°C for a duration of 8 h with a heating rate of 10°C min⁻¹. Following the hydrothermal treatment, the sample was allowed to cool to room temperature and then rinsed with water and subjected to freeze-drying.

nodes.source_text: Synthesis of NiFe LDH. The NiFe LDH was prepared by a one-step hydrothermal method. Typically, NiCl₂·6H₂O (3 mmol), Fe(NO₃)₃·9H₂O (1 mmol), urea (20 mmol), and NH₄F (10 mmol) were dissolved in 21 mL of water...

nodes.name: PO₄³⁻-modified NiFe LDH hydrothermal synthesis
nodes.procedure: The fabrication procedure of the PO₄³⁻-modified NiFe LDH catalyst (abbreviated as NiFe LDH-K₃PO₄) is akin to that of NiFe LDH, except for adding a different amount of K₃PO₄ (0.05, 1.0, 1.5, and 2.0 M). NiCl₂·6H₂O (3 mmol), Fe(NO₃)₃·9H₂O (1 mmol), urea (20 mmol), NH₄F (10 mmol), and K₃PO₄ (varying concentrations) were dissolved in 21 mL of water. Subsequently, the resulting mixture was transferred into a 30 mL Teflon-lined autoclave and subjected to heating in an oven at 120°C for a duration of 8 h with a heating rate of 10°C min⁻¹. Following the hydrothermal treatment, the sample was allowed to cool to room temperature and then rinsed with water and subjected to freeze-drying.

nodes.characterization_summary: NiFe LDH-K3PO4-2.0 M shows curly lamellar morphology; all NiFe LDH-K3PO4 samples show reduced nanosheet thickness compared to pristine NiFe LDH (~50 nm).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The SEM images of NiFe LDH-K3PO4-2.0 M (Figure S1) showed curly lamellar morphology... All of these morphology characterizations demonstrated that the introduced phosphate ions greatly reduced the thickness of LDH nanosheets...

nodes.characterization_summary: NiFe LDH-K3PO4 samples show ultrathin flaky polycrystalline nanosheet structure; pristine NiFe LDH shows plate-like shape.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The TEM image in Figure 1a displayed its ultrathin nanosheet structure with a thickness of 3-5 nm... For NiFe LDH-K3PO4-0.05 M (Figure S2) and NiFe LDH-K3PO4-1.0 M (Figure S3), they had a similar flaky and polycrystalline structure...

nodes.characterization_summary: Lattice fringes with 0.215 nm distance indexed to (018) plane of NiFe LDH for NiFe LDH-K3PO4-2.0 M.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 1b shows the high-resolution TEM (HR-TEM) image. The lattice fringes with a 0.215 nm distance can be indexed to the (018) plane of NiFe LDH.

nodes.characterization_summary: Uniform dispersion of Ni, Fe, P, O elements; P contents: 6.16 atom% (2.0 M), 4.62 atom% (1.0 M), 2.46 atom% (0.05 M).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The energy-dispersive spectroscopy (EDS) mapping (Figure 1c) showed the uniformly dispersed Ni, Fe, P, and O elements. The content of P in NiFe LDH-K3PO4-2.0 M was determined to be 6.16 atom %.

nodes.characterization_summary: Pristine NiFe LDH shows sharp peaks matching typical LDH structure (JCPDF 51-0463); NiFe LDH-K3PO4 samples show reduced peak intensities and negative shift of (003) peak indicating enlarged interlayer distance.
nodes.evidence_snippet: X-ray diffraction (XRD) patterns of the as-prepared samples (Figure 2a) showed that the sharp peaks of pristine NiFe LDH matched well with those of the typical LDH structure (JCPDF 51-0463), but the peak intensities of the NiFe LDH-K3PO4 samples were obviously reduced...

nodes.characterization_summary: P-O stretching vibration at ~1050 cm⁻¹ confirms PO₄³⁻ presence; replacement of interlayer CO₃²⁻ (1370 cm⁻¹) with phosphate anions.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The FTIR spectra (Figure 2b) verified the presence of PO₄³⁻ with the P-O stretching vibration located at around 1050 cm⁻¹ in the as-synthesized NiFe LDH-K3PO4 samples.

nodes.characterization_summary: NiFe LDH-K3PO4-2.0 M shows new peaks at 412 cm⁻¹ and 870-990 cm⁻¹ for phosphate vibrations; Ni-O and Fe-O modes at 459, 538, 303 cm⁻¹.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Figure 2c, two peaks at 459 and 538 cm⁻¹ correspond to Ni²⁺-O bending... In contrast, a new sharp peak at 412 cm⁻¹ and a broad peak at around 870-990 cm⁻¹ appeared in NiFe LDH-K3PO4-2.0 M, which were indexed to the vibrational modes of the phosphate ion.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni 2p shifts: pristine 856.2 eV → 856.6 eV (0.05M,1.0M) → 855.8 eV (2.0M); P 2p at 133.1 eV; oxygen vacancy ratios increase from 32.1% (pristine) to 40.7% (2.0M).
nodes.evidence_snippet: X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) was further carried out to determine the surface electronic structure... the high-resolution Ni 2p XPS spectrum of pristine NiFe LDH displayed Ni 2p₃/₂ and 2p₁/₂ peaks at 856.2 and 874.3 eV...

nodes.characterization_summary: Double-layer capacitance Cdl values from CV at various scan rates: NiFe LDH 1.53 mF cm⁻², NiFe LDH-K3PO4-0.05 M 1.89 mF cm⁻², 1.0 M 1.63 mF cm⁻², 2.0 M 1.66 mF cm⁻².
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Cdl values of NiFe LDH-K3PO4-0.05 M (1.89 mF cm⁻²), NiFe LDH-K3PO4-1.0 M (1.63 mF cm⁻²), and NiFe LDH-K3PO4-2.0 M (1.66 mF cm⁻²) were larger than that of NiFe LDH (1.53 mF cm⁻²) in Figure 3d.

nodes.characterization_summary: Rct values: 2.06 Ω (NiFe LDH), 0.31 Ω (0.05M), 0.21 Ω (1.0M), 0.88 Ω (2.0M) indicating improved conductivity.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Nyquist plots (Figure S13) showed that pristine NiFe LDH had the largest charge transfer resistance (Rct) of 2.06 Ω... The Rct value of NiFe LDH-K3PO4-2.0 M (0.88 Ω) was higher than those of NiFe LDH-K3PO4-0.05 M (0.31 Ω) and NiFe LDH-K3PO4-1.0 M (0.21 Ω).
